**Answer (according to the “Experiencing Violence” section of the 2013‑2023 YRBSS Data Summary & Trends Report on wonder.cdc.gov)**  

| Youth‑Risk‑Behavior Category (All Years Available) | Trend direction | Trend details |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Any physical assault** | *Increasing* | The percentage of middle‑ and high‑school students reporting that they had been physically attacked (pushed, slapped, hit, kicked, or otherwise physically harmed) in the past 12 months rose steadily from 2013 to 2023. |
| **2. Serious injury from violence** | *Increasing* | The percentage of students reporting that a physical assault had caused a serious injury (e.g., a broken bone, serious cut, or head injury) increased across the decade. |
| **3. Sexual victimization** | *Increasing* | The rate of students who reported that they had been forced or pressured into sexual activities (including rape, coerced sexual contact, or being forced to have sex) climbed over the 10‑year span. |
| **4. Physical dating violence** | *Increasing* | The proportion of students who reported being physically harmed by a dating partner (pushed, slapped, hit, or otherwise physically harmed) rose markedly from 2013 to 2023. |

**Explanation of “Wrong Direction”**

The CDC’s YRBSS reports present trends for each victimization indicator. When a trend line is shown in *red* on the “Trend (All Years Available)” chart, that indicates that the behavior is “trending in the wrong direction”—i.e., it has risen (or declined in a preventable minority of cases) across the decade. In the 2013‑2023 summary, the four indicators listed above are the only ones that show the **increasing** trend that denotes a worsening public‑health situation for adolescents.

*These four trends are the sole “red‑trend” items identified in the Experiencing‑Violence section of the 2013‑2023 YRBSS Data Summary & Trends Report available on the CDC Wonder portal.*
